title: Combining Conditions with and, or, and not
content:
What problem does this solve?
Some doors need two keys at once — a physical key and enough gold. Boolean operators combine smaller yes/no questions into one condition.

Basic syntax
  if has_key and gold >= 10:
      print("enter")

  if health < 20 or enemies >= 3:
      print("flee")

What actually happens
and requires every part to be true. or needs at least one part true. not flips a boolean. Python also allows chained comparisons such as 0 < health <= 100 — one readable range check.

When this is useful
Combine requirements (key and gold), escape triggers (low health or too many foes), or flip a flag with not.
concepts: or needs at least one sub-condition true
Chained comparisons such as 0 < health <= 100 test a range in one expression

examples.title: Gate requires key and gold
examples.explanation: Both has_key and enough gold are true, so enter prints.

examples.title: Flee when overwhelmed
examples.explanation: enemies >= 3 is true, so or makes the whole condition true.

common_mistakes: Using = instead of == inside a condition
Assuming English or means only one option — logical or is true if either side is true
Forgetting that and stops early when the first part is false

exercises.title: Trace and and or
exercises.prompt: Decide what prints. Trace each sub-condition before you answer, then click Check.
exercises.failure_message: has_key is true, but is gold >= 10 true when gold is 8? and needs both sides true.
hints: Evaluate has_key first — is it true?
Now check gold >= 10 with gold equal to 8.
When one side of and is false, the whole condition is false.

exercises.title: Predict with not
exercises.prompt: What prints? Trace how not flips the condition, then click Check.
exercises.failure_message: not has_key is true when has_key is False — the if branch runs.
hints: has_key is False.
not False becomes True.
The if branch prints blocked.

exercises.title: Complete the flee condition
exercises.prompt: Print flee when health is below 20 OR enemies is at least 3. Replace None with the correct or expression.
exercises.starter_code:
health = 30
enemies = 3
if None:  # TODO: low health OR too many enemies
    print("flee")
else:
    print("fight")
hints: You need two comparisons joined by or.
One side checks health; the other checks enemies.
Try health < 20 or enemies >= 3.

tests.message: Use if / else with a compound condition.

exercises.title: Fix the gate check
exercises.prompt:
This gate program should print enter when the passphrase matches "open", but it crashes with a SyntaxError. The bug is using = where a comparison belongs.

Run the code to read the error, fix the condition, then Check.
hints: Run first — Python will point at the if line.
Inside a condition you compare values; = assigns.
Use == to test whether entered equals passphrase.

tests.message: Fix the condition to compare with ==, not =.

exercises.title: Gate entry requirements
exercises.prompt:
Write can_enter(has_key, gold) that returns True only when the explorer has the key AND at least 10 gold.

Return a boolean — do not print. Both requirements must be satisfied.
exercises.success_message: You combined and with comparisons in a reusable function — the same gate logic you will see in shops and dungeons later.
hints: Think of two separate questions: key? enough gold?
Join them with and inside one return statement.
Both has_key and gold >= 10 must be true.
return has_key and gold >= 10

tests.message: When has_key is True and gold is 15, entry should be allowed.
Exactly 10 gold with a key should still allow entry.
A key alone is not enough — 9 gold should block entry.
Gold without a key should not allow entry.
Any gold amount at or above 10 with a key should allow entry.
11 gold with a key should allow entry — not only the examples from the prompt.
Neither requirement met should return False.

exercises.title: Inclusive health range
exercises.prompt: Print valid when health is between 0 and 100 inclusive. Replace None with a condition that passes for health 0, 50, and 100.
exercises.starter_code:
health = 100
if None:  # TODO: 0 through 100 inclusive
    print("valid")
else:
    print("invalid")
hints: Inclusive means 0 and 100 should both pass.
You can write health >= 0 and health <= 100.
Chained 0 < health < 100 would reject the endpoints.

tests.message: Use a comparison that includes both endpoints.

exercises.title: Readable range check
exercises.prompt: You want to verify that health stayed between 0 and 100 inclusive. Which condition is clearest and correct in Python?
exercises.success_message: Correct — and health <= 100 includes 100. The chained form 0 < health < 100 excludes both endpoints.
exercises.failure_message: 0 < health < 100 rejects health of exactly 0 or 100. To include both endpoints you need <= and >=.
hints: Ask whether health of exactly 0 or 100 should pass.
Chained comparisons exclude the endpoints here.
Pick the condition that includes both 0 and 100.
